name: Procyon Energy Station
summary: The grid of Procyon City: four heat-pipe fission modules of about 5 MWe each run around the clock, and a 12 MWp photovoltaic field adds power by day. Dust in the air cuts the solar output, most of all in a dust storm.

kpis.label: Total generation
kpis.note: design is the sol average: 19.6 MW fission plus about 4 MW solar

kpis.label: Solar output
kpis.note: design is the sol average of a 12 MWp field in clear weather

since_note: About 2078: the colonies were nuclear-led by 2080.
story: Dust storms in spring and autumn hurt the early solar plants, so IIA built wind and nuclear stations. By 2080 the colonies ran on nuclear power, with wind and solar in support.
process: Four heat-pipe microreactors (about 15 MWt each) with closed Brayton converters, 34 % efficient
Control drums hold the core outlet at 650 degC; each module is refuelled and inspected about every 300 days
12 MWp photovoltaic field; output follows the sol and the dust optical depth
